This textbook is a self-study resource for the theoretical component of the
course **Web Application Development I** (DAW1), Bachelor's in
Communication and Multimedia, covering server-side web application
development with PHP, from the fundamentals of client-server communication
to the architecture and security of modern web applications.

In the practical component of the course, students apply these concepts by
building dynamic web sites with PHP and databases. This textbook covers the
theoretical component; the practical component is covered separately, in
the corresponding classes.

## Organisation {.unnumbered}

The text is organised into five thematic blocks, following the course's
official syllabus:

1. **Web Foundations and Landscape** — chapters 1 and 2, covering the
   process of developing a web application and the different types of
   servers and infrastructure
2. **PHP Programming** — chapters 3, 4 and 5, covering syntax, control
   flow, functions and code organisation
3. **Communication and State on the Web** — in this block, chapters 6 and
   7, network models, the HTTP protocol, and state management with cookies
   and sessions
4. **Data and Security** — this block covers chapters 8 and 9, on
   databases with PHP and web application security
5. **Architecture and Tools** — finally, this block, chapters 10 and 11,
   covers the Model-View-Controller pattern and web development frameworks

## Source and Updates {.unnumbered}

The content of this textbook is based on the lecturer's own material,
developed over previous years of teaching the course (slides and code
demonstrations), reorganised and updated for the 2026/2027 academic year.
The reference bibliography for the course is listed in each chapter and
compiled in the `referencias.bib` file.

## How to Use This Textbook {.unnumbered}

Each chapter corresponds to one theoretical class of the course. Students
are advised to read a chapter before the corresponding class, and to use
this text as support for independent study, to review concepts and
clarify doubts. Reading does not replace attendance in class, nor
participation in the practical, in-class demonstrations.
In every chapter involving PHP programming, the example code is presented
directly in the text, and students are encouraged to experiment with the
code, testing it and modifying it to better understand the concepts,
through the challenges proposed at the end of each chapter.
